speaker: EVA
direction: to the phone, quiet, the whole site still asleep
line: Day nineteen.

speaker: EVA
line: Sun's not up. Ishita's not up. The monsoon is three weeks early and nobody at the Institute wants to talk about what that does to a trench.

speaker: EVA
line: But you lot didn't come here for drainage.

speaker: EVA
direction: turning the camera to the pit
line: You came for this.

speaker: EVA
line: Dholarath. Four and a half thousand years old. Grid streets, covered drains, a reservoir that could hold a season of rain —

speaker: EVA
line: — and a writing system that nobody on Earth can read.

speaker: EVA
line: Four hundred signs. Thousands of inscriptions. Not one of them understood.

speaker: EVA
line: Thirty years ago somebody worked out why. She said: stop reading it like a language. It isn't sentences. It's an index — labels, pointing

speaker: EVA
line: at something that isn't the writing.

speaker: EVA
line: The field laughed her out of the room.

speaker: EVA
line: She's my mother. So, you know. Personal stake.

speaker: ISHITA
line: Two million people and you still can't operate a kettle.

speaker: EVA
line: Two million people fund your remote sensing, Dr Vaid.

speaker: ISHITA
line: Two million people think you found a "lost city." You found a well-documented site with a new trench in it.

speaker: EVA
line: Two million people have hope. You should try it.

speaker: ISHITA
line: ...What am I looking at?

speaker: EVA
line: That's what I'm asking you. You're the one with the ground scans.

speaker: ISHITA
line: When you find Atlantis, wake me.

speaker: EVA
line: Rude.

speaker: EVA
line: Right. Slowly. We don't take, we record.

speaker: EVA
direction: a beat, to herself, almost ritual
line: Brush, don't scrape. Dad's rule.

speaker: EVA
line: Oh, hello.

speaker: EVA
direction: holding it up to the lens
line: Potsherd. Red slip. Probably a storage jar, probably nothing, probably the single most beautiful nothing you'll

speaker: EVA
line: see today.

speaker: SAKSHI
line: You're in the trench.

speaker: EVA
line: How do you always —

speaker: SAKSHI
line: Because it's five in the morning and you're whispering.

speaker: EVA
line: Ma.

speaker: SAKSHI
line: What did you find?

speaker: EVA
line: Red slip sherd. And the floor's wrong. It's too flat, and it's too flat in a straight line.

speaker: SAKSHI
line: Check the drainage, beta. Not the walls. Everyone always checks the walls.

speaker: SAKSHI
line: I told the reviewers that in '98 and they laughed at me for an hour.

speaker: EVA
line: I know, Ma.

speaker: SAKSHI
line: Don't "I know" me. Go and look at the drain.

speaker: EVA
line: Okay, so this is — this is probably a kerb stone, these run along the —

speaker: EVA
line: That's a lintel.

speaker: ISHITA
line: Eva. That's a door.

speaker: EVA
line: I know it's a door.

speaker: ISHITA
line: That's a *sealed* door.

speaker: EVA
direction: not to the phone any more
line: Ma was right.

speaker: EVA
line: There's someone in here.

speaker: EVA
line: Sitting up. Not buried — *placed*. Facing the door.

speaker: EVA
line: And the whole back wall is covered in signs.

speaker: EVA
line: I can't read any of it. Nobody can read any of it.

speaker: EVA
line: Except — (stopping) Except that pairing. There, and there, and — six times.

speaker: EVA
line: That's the pairing off the north gate signboard.

speaker: EVA
line: The one every tourist photograph in Gujarat has in the background.

speaker: EVA
line: It's a label. It's labelling something.

speaker: EVA
line: It's an *index*.

speaker: EVA
line: And you're holding something.

speaker: EVA
line: Copper. Disc. Eight spokes.

speaker: EVA
line: I should not touch this. I should photograph this, and log this, and call it in, and not touch this.

speaker: EVA
line: Recorded. Logged. Witnessed.

speaker: EVA
line: Okay.

speaker: EVA
line: It's warm.

speaker: EVA
line: Why is it warm —

speaker: EVA
line: What.

speaker: VASUDHA
line: Late.

speaker: VASUDHA
line: You Keepers are always late.
